title: Re-indent a pasted snippet

blocks.text: The page offers two methods that bring the text block rules to any string: `stripIndent()` applies the compiler's incidental whitespace algorithm (where a blank last line counts, like a closing delimiter on its own line), and `indent(n)` adds `n` spaces to every line. Its best practices use them together to place generated code at the right depth.
Write `Snippet.nest(String code, int level)`. `code` is a snippet pasted with any indentation and any line endings. Return it re-based at `level`:

items: the snippet's common indentation is removed, its inner indentation kept, and spaces at the end of each line are removed;
a **blank** line (empty, or only spaces, the last line included) takes no part in the common indentation;
every non-blank line is then indented by `4 * level` spaces, and a blank line stays **empty**;
every line ends with `\n`, the last one included, and line endings are `\n` only.

blocks.text: (`·` is a space.) `level` is never negative, and `code` has at least one non-blank line.

cases.says: The snippet loses its common indentation, keeps its inner indentation, and every line is indented four spaces per level and ends with \n.
A blank line in the snippet stays an empty line, with no spaces added to it.
A line of only spaces is blank and takes no part in the common indentation, even with fewer spaces than the others.
At level 0 the snippet is only re-based, and its last line still ends with \n.
A snippet with \r\n line endings comes out with \n only.
Spaces at the end of a line are removed, as the text block algorithm does.

concepts: indent(n) adds n spaces to every line, blank ones included, normalizes line endings and always ends the result with \n, even for indent(0).
stripIndent() applies the text block algorithm to any string: common indentation and trailing whitespace go, line terminators become \n.
Trailing whitespace on each line is stripped by default.
